initial_requirements: Vrije Universiteit Brussel needs a Publications Management System for storing bibliographic records and full publication texts. Users with different roles should be able to search, upload, download, correct, and moderate publication information according to their access rights. The system should extract bibliographic details from documents, support bulk imports, and help reconcile alternative names that refer to the same author or institution.

topics.topic_content: User roles and access responsibilities in the repository

slots.key: Defined user roles and permissions
slots.value: Researchers or delegated staff can enter or update records; only authorized library or repository staff can approve and finalize them. Until approval, records are drafts or pending versions and not authoritative; after approval, the approved version becomes the one everyone relies on. For pending records, the submitter or repository staff can usually propose changes more freely; after approval, corrections should come from authorized staff or the original contributor if they have the proper role; if a record is later found to be inaccurate, repository staff can intervene directly as a data quality issue. Staff should be able to correct metadata, merge duplicate author or institution names, approve or reject pending records, run or re-run bulk imports, and fix common issues like missing fields, wrong classifications, or attaching the right full text, as long as it stays within their role. Technical support only needs to step in for system errors, failed integrations, import format problems staff cannot interpret, or workflow blocks outside the normal publication process. The system should prefill fields from the document, let a staff member review and correct them before finalization, clearly mark uncertain or ambiguous extraction so the reviewer knows what needs attention, and when there is a conflict with an existing record it should compare the records side by side and flag a possible duplicate or mismatch, with the final decision staying with the moderator. When users are searching, they should be able to refine the search and browse related records, and if that still fails they should have a fallback lookup path such as alternate author names, institution variants, or identifiers. Access or record status should limit what is shown if the publication is restricted or still under review, but the system should still indicate that a record exists when the user is allowed to know that.

topics.topic_content: Terminology and entity definitions for publications and contributors

slots.key: Core bibliographic terms and field meanings
slots.value: The repository is a reliable central record of all VUB publications, including publication texts and metadata, used for internal reporting, easier discovery and reuse, visibility, compliance, and performance reporting. For each record it stores basic bibliographic metadata such as title, authors, affiliations, publication date, journal or conference details, DOI or other identifiers, and publication type; it also stores full text files when available, linked clearly to the correct bibliographic record. A publication may have several related files (for example, a submitted version and a final version), and those relationships should be kept clear rather than treating the files as separate unrelated entries.

slots.key: Definition of author, institution, and affiliation variants
slots.value: It handles cases where the same author or institution appears under different names, but author name variants must not be merged automatically just because they look similar. Different spellings or forms should only be treated as the same author with an approved authority record or manual confirmation, to avoid collapsing distinct people, especially with common names or transliterated forms. The system should keep the source form in the record, but also normalize it into a standard authority form when we have a confirmed match. If there isn’t enough confidence, it should keep them separate and flag them for review rather than forcing a normalization. For organizations, the same principle applies, especially when abbreviations or language variants could refer to different entities.

If the evidence is weak or conflicting, the record should stay unresolved and be routed to a more experienced reviewer or escalated for manual checking.

topics.topic_content: Access-control rules for publication data and files

slots.key: Role-based permissions for search, upload, correction, and moderation
slots.value: Users with different roles can search, upload, download, correct, and moderate publication information according to their access rights; researchers or delegated staff can enter or update records, but only authorized library or repository staff can approve and finalize them. For correction proposals, pending records can usually be changed more freely by the submitter or repository staff; after approval, corrections should come from authorized staff or the original contributor if they have the proper role; if a record is later found to be inaccurate, repository staff can intervene directly. For routine corrections, staff can correct metadata, merge duplicate author or institution names, approve or reject pending records, run or re-run bulk imports, and fix common problems like missing fields, wrong classifications, or attaching the right full text as long as it stays within their role. Technical support only needs to step in for system errors, failed integrations, import format problems staff cannot interpret, or workflows blocked by something outside the normal publication process. Staff may edit normal bibliographic fields and moderate records that are still in draft, pending, or otherwise not yet finalized; once a record is approved or published, changes to key fields or attached full text should require a second review, especially if the change affects the public record or reporting; if staff cannot resolve a conflict, they should be able to flag it for another moderator or escalate it to a higher authority rather than guessing. The system should prefill extracted fields from the document, let staff check and correct them before finalization, clearly mark uncertain or ambiguous parts for review, and when a conflict with an existing record appears it should support side-by-side comparison and flag a possible duplicate or mismatch, while the final decision stays with the moderator.

slots.key: Draft status before approval for publication records
slots.value: Until approval, the record should be treated as a draft or pending version, not the authoritative one; while draft or pending, access should be limited to the contributor, repository staff, and moderators with the right access, with editing restricted to the people responsible for that record and downloading the attached files also limited so unfinished or unapproved material is not exposed broadly. Any temporary circulation must be exceptional and tied to a specific review purpose, not a normal workflow.

slots.key: Default sorting and filtering for publication record browsing
slots.value: Staff would generally want the most recent or most recently updated records first, but for staff who are actively processing items, their own pending records should be surfaced first by default. The rule is to prioritize items assigned to them or items they created that are still pending, then fall back to the normal recency sort. Users should also be able to refine the search and browse related records; if that still fails, the repository should provide a fallback lookup path using alternate author names, institution variants, or identifiers. If a publication is restricted or still under review, access or record status should limit what is shown, but the system should still indicate that a record exists when the user is allowed to know that.

topics.topic_content: Rules for normalizing names and reconciling equivalent entities

slots.key: Authority control rules for author name variants
slots.value: Do not merge name variants automatically just because they look similar; require an approved authority record or at least manual confirmation before treating different spellings or forms as the same author, to avoid collapsing distinct people, especially with common names or transliterated forms. Keep the source form in the record, but normalize it into a standard authority form when there is a confirmed match; if confidence is not sufficient, keep records separate and flag them for review rather than forcing normalization. For similar-looking matches, do not auto-link unless confidence is high and the matching rules are very clear; otherwise leave them unnormalized and send them to manual review. Auto-link only for agreed-safe cases such as exact variants or well-known standardized abbreviations. Auto-linking should be limited to cases where the match is essentially deterministic, like an exact normalized variant, a known abbreviation that’s already approved, or a transliteration that maps unambiguously to one authority form. If there is any real ambiguity, especially with common abbreviations or names that could belong to more than one person or institution, it should go to manual review.

slots.key: Name normalization and entity matching rules
slots.value: Keep the source form in the record, but also normalize it into a standard authority form only when there is a confirmed match or the confidence is high enough and the matching rules are very clear. Auto-linking should be limited to cases that are essentially deterministic, such as an exact normalized variant, a known abbreviation already approved, or a transliteration that maps unambiguously to one authority form. If there is any real ambiguity, especially with common abbreviations or names that could belong to more than one person or institution, do not auto-link; send it to manual review. Apply the same conservative principle to organizations, especially when abbreviations or language variants could refer to different entities.
